topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): add flashblocks-aware routing
topPRs.author: paranoiacblack
topPRs.body:
**Description**

- Adds flashblocks-aware routing. When `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `eth_getTransactionCount`, `eth_getTransactionReceipt` and `eth_getBalance` are called with "pending" block numbers on chains producing Flashblocks, the request will be answered by a flashblocks-aware backend.
- Adds configuration that enables flashblocks-aware routing.
- Adds configuration that allows specifying exactly one flashblocks-aware backend group.
- Adds logic to parse JSON-RPC request's method and parameters to determine if it should be sent to the flashblocks-aware backend group or to normally configured backend group for the rpc method mapping. 

**Tests**

- Added tests for checking for pending JSON-RPC requests.
- Added integration tests for every request + param combination that can ask for information about the latest flashblock.

topPRs.title: ci: release Go binaries from GitHub Actions
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Add a `release-go-binaries` GitHub Actions workflow. It runs on `<module>/v*` tags for `op-signer`, `op-txproxy`, `op-ufm`, `proxyd`, `op-conductor-mon`, `peer-mgmt-service` and `cci-stats`, and on `workflow_dispatch` for an existing tag.
- The build job runs with read-only permissions and builds the archives and `<module>_<version>_checksums.txt` for linux/amd64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64. The publish job has `contents: write` and runs no repository code. It only attaches the uploaded artifacts to a draft release and then publishes it.
- Archive and checksum names are the same as before.
- Behaviour changes: binaries are static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`). Versions with a `-` suffix are marked as prereleases. Release notes are the module's commit log since its previous tag. `op-txproxy` releases are not marked as latest.
- Remove the CircleCI `go-release` job and its release workflow, along with the seven per-module `.goreleaser.yaml` files. `RELEASE.md` is updated to describe the tag-driven process.

topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): add auth label to latency, cache and HTTP status metrics
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Per-API-key observability already exists on nine metrics via the `auth` label (the alias configured in `[authentication]`, or `none`). This extends it to the remaining request-scoped metrics so latency, cache hit rate and HTTP status can be filtered per key:

- `proxyd_http_request_by_method_duration_seconds` (`method_name`, `auth`)
- `proxyd_cache_hits_total` / `proxyd_cache_misses_total` (`method`, `auth`)
- `proxyd_http_response_codes_total` (`status_code`, `auth`)

Unauthenticated and rejected (401) requests carry `auth="none"`, same as the existing metrics.

### Cardinality
Each metric gains one series per configured key alias. For the latency histogram that is methods × keys × 12 buckets, so fine for tens of keys; worth reconsidering for hundreds.

### Dashboards
Existing queries keep working since `auth` is additive, but any panel that does not aggregate (`sum by (...)`) will now show one line per key.

## Test plan
- New `TestHTTPRequestByMethodDurationAuthLabel` asserts an authenticated request lands in the `auth="alice"` series for both the histogram and the status counter.
- Existing tests pinned to `auth="none"` so superset label matching stays unambiguous.
- `go test ./...` passes in `proxyd/`.

topPRs.title: fix(proxyd): rate limit method override semantics
topPRs.author: yashvardhan-kukreja
topPRs.body:
Signed-off-by: Yashvardhan Kukreja <yashvardhan@oplabs.co>

<!-- Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

**Description**

The rate-limit-method-overrides never overrode the base rate-limits. Instead they applied on top of the base-rate-limits. That doesn't make much sense with the concept of "overrides" and makes it impossible to loosen the rate limit of a specific method compared to the base rate.

This PR fixes that by either applying the base-rate-limit on the incoming request OR the method-override if it exists for the incoming request's RPC method.
